note: Saved by the orchestrator from the agent's returned JSON; the full reactions list is condensed to the scored and actionable parts.

first_impression.why: The intro describes us exactly (around 90 guests, Instagram-perfect shortlist, planning from Sydney) and names the 11pm worry: who answers in March, who is at the gates, where the deposits go.

strongest_passages: The planner-types table ('Works for the venue, not for you')
7pm Sydney call lands 9am to 11am in Italy; reply time written into the contract
The supplier-payment question, the questions table with good answers and warning signs, references from overseas couples
Heat facts, SIAE licence detail, dated legal sources, English contract terms

fears_coverage.fear: Hiring the wrong planner (polished, unreliable, kickbacks)
Planning from the other side of the world
Spending a lot and still getting generic, or overcharged as foreigners
Losing control of the budget across currencies and Italian contracts

unanswered_questions: What will a full planner realistically cost for 90 guests over three days?
How far ahead do we need to book? We are 12 to 18 months out.
How does Wedded Wonderland make money? Do partnered planners pay a referral fee?
What exactly are partnered planners vetted for?
Who would we actually speak to?
What does the concierge cost us, if anything?
Lock in exchange rates, forex account, or pay as we go?
Do Italian vendors charge foreign couples more?
payload.in_their_words: Honestly the most useful thing I've read on this. The questions table and the partita IVA check are things I'll actually use. But they tell me to ask every planner whether suppliers pay them, and then never say whether their partnered network pays them. And there's a note to someone called Nic in the middle of the fees section. Saving it, not calling yet.
